clue.text: Excessively self-satisfied Southern simpleton

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool, a simpleton

explanation.surface: A sneer at a complacent fool from the South.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smug is complacently pleased with themselves, too much so.

clue.text: Ecstasy over Republican tirade going wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: E is slang shorthand for the drug ecstasy
a rant is a long angry tirade

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled harangue at a Republican goes off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, erring or wandering astray.

clue.text: Weakened and confused dupes frequently taken in

indicators.note: taken in says one piece is held inside the other
confused letters are jumbled, so the word dupes is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
frequently means often

explanation.surface: Fools muddled and repeatedly conned end up weaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weakened and confused' reads as one description, but only 'Weakened' defines; 'confused' makes SEDUP, which 'taken in' splits after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To be softened up is to be weakened in resistance before an attack or a sales pitch.

clue.text: Voted as directed, supporting three political leaders

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second
three asks for not one but the first three letters of the following word
leaders are the front letters of the word political

parts.note: led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: Someone cast their ballot as instructed, backing three party chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three ... leaders' takes POL, the first three letters of 'political'; 'supporting' puts LED below it. 'as' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be polled is to have one's vote taken or registered, so it can mean voted.

clue.text: Awfully odd spiel, far from balanced

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly done, so odd spiel is rearranged

explanation.surface: A terribly strange speech that is hardly even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided means uneven or tilted to one side, the opposite of balanced.

clue.text: Even part of state supporting main goal of politician

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece is underneath, so it comes last

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: an even part is a letter in an even-numbered position of the word state

explanation.surface: A politician's aim, apparently propped up by an even share of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even part of state' picks a T, one of the second and fourth letters of STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning a seat in a legislature is what an election candidate aims for.

clue.text: Bizarre muddle I clear up

indicators.note: to muddle is to mix up, so I clear up is rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange mess that the speaker tidies away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' looks like a noun I clear up, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar and bizarre are synonyms, both meaning strange or odd.

clue.text: Placed above all the other politicians, initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words that come before it

explanation.surface: A candidate ranked higher than every rival politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, positioned above something else.

clue.text: Noted explorer making name once in US politics and sport

parts.note: Marco Rubio was a contender for the 2016 Republican nomination
polo is a sport played on horseback

explanation.surface: A famous traveller seems to have built a name in American politics and games.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco Rubio had just dropped out of the 2016 Republican primaries when this ran.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian traveller who reached Kublai Khan's China is among history's best-known explorers.

clue.text: To do this, people will choose Democratic president, ultimately?

definitions.text: To do this, people will choose Democratic president, ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Voters will, in the end, pick a Democrat as president.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the act and also supplies its letters from the last of five words.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose a president by voting is exactly what people do when they vote someone into office.

clue.text: Present or past president

definitions.meaning: a present is a gift or award given to someone
Ulysses S. ... was the eighteenth US president

explanation.surface: A gift, or a former leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is something bestowed, and Grant led the Union army before becoming US president.

clue.text: Ultimate demagogue that will usher in day of reckoning

definitions.text: that will usher in day of reckoning

parts.note: ultimate means final, last
Donald Trump, then a rabble-rousing presidential candidate

explanation.surface: A final rabble-rouser who will bring on judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition a final trumpet call sounds to announce Judgement Day.

clue.text: Hit one Democrat, struck with club

parts.note: to bat is to hit, as with a bat

explanation.surface: Someone hits a Democrat and clubs them.
explanation.definitionFit: Batoned means beaten with a truncheon, a policeman's club.

clue.text: Run, in part, as epitome of intolerance

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
to go can mean to run, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Someone running partly on a platform of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run, in part' reads as a phrase, but it is GO placed in BIT; 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is the archetype of a narrow-minded, prejudiced person.

clue.text: One looking good around Southern state that's not all white

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
Ark is an abbreviation for Arkansas, a state in the American South

explanation.surface: An attractive person in a Southern state that isn't completely white.
explanation.definitionFit: Something darkish is somewhat dark in colour, hence not wholly pale or white.

clue.text: Adherent of middle line? Yes and no

definitions.text: Adherent of middle line? Yes and no

parts.words: Adherent of middle line? Yes and no
parts.note: a supporter of a party that is one of two main US parties, centre stage in one sense but hardly middle-of-the-road politically

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about someone who supports a moderate position.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger was unsure of the intended reading; the question mark and 'Yes and no' signal a teasing description rather than wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Grand Old Party is a member of one of the two main American political parties.

clue.text: It's hard getting votes for 11's successor

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
ayes are votes in favour

explanation.surface: Getting votes is tough work.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' points to GRANT at 11 across, the president Ulysses S. Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutherford B. Hayes followed Ulysses Grant as US president in 1877.

clue.text: Good article penned by Republican and Democrat for a lot of dollars

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, as in a pen, by the following pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece written jointly by members of both parties in return for big money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a thousand dollars, which is a lot of money.

clue.text: Absurdly lauded over a time, praised excessively

indicators.note: over is read as covering, the jumbled letters wrapping round the rest
absurdly suggests the word lauded is set in a ridiculous new order

explanation.surface: Praised ridiculously for a while, overpraised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurdly' turns LAUDED into ADULED; 'over' has it wrap around A and T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate someone is to flatter or worship them beyond what they deserve.

clue.text: Veteran from left in party getting backed

indicators.note: getting backed means turned back to front, so the letters are read in reverse
in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An old soldier leaves his party and is supported in return.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone old and experienced, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Utter what's inaccurate, supported by conservatives

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supported by another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a guess that is out is wrong or inaccurate
the right is the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: Speak falsehoods with the backing of conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, to say, but it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and outright both mean complete or total, as in an utter or outright lie.

clue.text: Kind of animal that's associated with elephant or donkey, for example?

definitions.meaning: a ... animal is someone who loves socialising and nightlife

definitions.text: that's associated with elephant or donkey, for example?
definitions.meaning: the elephant symbolises the Republicans and the donkey the Democrats

explanation.surface: A zoology question about elephants and donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Each US political grouping has a mascot beast, and a reveller is a party animal.

clue.text: Something blown by itself to a large extent

definitions.text: Something blown by itself to a large extent

parts.words: Something blown by itself to a large extent
parts.note: a brass instrument that is blown, whose name is mostly the surname of a boastful candidate, who blows his own horn

explanation.surface: Describing something that inflates itself enormously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by itself to a large extent' hints that most of the word is the candidate's surname, a man famous for self-promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument is played by blowing into it, and to blow one's own horn is to boast.

clue.text: Base Ted excited in arguments with opponents

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so Base Ted is rearranged

explanation.surface: Ted Cruz fires up the party base in clashes with rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted points to Ted Cruz, a 2016 candidate, but here is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Debates are formal arguments between opposing speakers.

clue.text: Love going after Mitt's likely successor, animated character

indicators.note: going after places the first piece behind the second

parts.note: Donald Trump, likely to follow Mitt Romney as Republican nominee
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, and love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Romance follows the man expected to take over from Romney.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's irascible cartoon duck is one of the best known animated characters.

clue.text: Finally shout like a crazy, not silent

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word shout
crazy suggests the letters of like a are jumbled

explanation.surface: At last somebody yells like a madman, refusing to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' turns LIKE A into ALKIE. The answer is a film with sound, so the definition reads 'not silent (film)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Early sound films were called talkies to distinguish them from silent pictures.

clue.text: On air, can broadcast after Democrat, showing extreme harshness

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the earlier piece
broadcast suggests scattering, so On air, can is rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcaster follows a Democrat with a brutally severe message.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian, from the harsh Athenian lawgiver Draco, means excessively severe.

clue.text: See 22
Throw out Obamacare using salami tactics, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each preceding word

explanation.surface: Scrap the health law bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Salami tactics means achieving something by removing small slices at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to expel or remove someone or something.

clue.text: Look into one attempt to get White House?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a go is an attempt
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Examine one bid to win the presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' is not the president's home but a house made of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow dwelling is literally a white house.

clue.text: Some loathsome characters that incoming president has to take

definitions.text: that incoming president has to take

indicators.note: some ... characters says only part of the following word's letters are taken

explanation.surface: A newly elected leader must accept some horrible people.
explanation.definitionFit: An incoming US president must swear the oath of office at inauguration.

clue.text: Gangs uttered name of ex-runner

indicators.note: uttered says the word is spoken, so it is about how it sounds

parts.note: Ted Cruz had just left the race for the Republican nomination

explanation.surface: Gangs spoke the name of a former candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crews and gangs are both groups of people working together.

clue.text: Plan cobbled together with faith that's small beer

indicators.note: cobbled together means roughly assembled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan thrown together on faith that turns out trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a small measure of beer; small beer is also an idiom for someone or something unimportant.
